correctness.rationale: One occurrence per required equal-length word, sorted by start position, gives a lower bound by overlap costs; appending with those maximal overlaps attains that length for a given order. Within a rotation class the least positive shift d gives overlap 5p−d, irrespective of p≥2. Between different classes every overlap has length at most four, determined by the root boundaries. An order using B cross-class edges has length at least 5p+31+5(p−1)B, with B≥7; if B≥8 the lower bound 45p−9 exceeds 40p+2 throughout p≥3. An independent reproduction at p=3 built literal suffix/prefix costs and used a root-level remaining-set recurrence: from a current root, if any unvisited root in its class remains, the next root must be one of these; otherwise any remaining root is allowed. This recurrence enumerates exactly the grouped permutations and yielded minimum 122 over 61696 memoized states. The literal 122-bit witness contains all 32 cubes. A grouped route has length increment 40 per exponent because its seven cross-class edges and initial length each increase by five; thus both the all-exponent optimum and the restriction on all optimal orders follow.
residual_risks: This verifies the finite linear-word optimization, not an analogous circular or general root-length problem. The certificate histogram lists only the seven nonterminal layers; 32 terminal endpoints bring the total from 4064 to 4096.

evidence: The exact square minimum is 82 over all permutations, attained at seven class switches. Every permutation has B≥7, and its length at exponent p is its length at exponent 2 plus 5(p−2)(B+1).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Every order costs at least 82+40(p−2)=40p+2, and a grouped square minimizer realizes equality at every p≥3. Since p−2>0, any B>7 forces strict inequality. Both frozen conclusions therefore follow without solving the cubic DP. Au alone also implies grouping: at B≥8 the cost is at least 45p−9, above his available upper bound.
